en: Warehouse lead: clear the seconds shelf
Hello {lead}, the {area} needs clearing. Please grade the items, price the sellable seconds and list what must be written off.
Picker and packer: count a shelf
Hello {lead}, please count {area} today and write the quantities on the count sheet.
Picker and packer: move to the pick zone
Hello {keeper}, please move {product} to the pick zone, bin {pick_bin}. It has {pick_units} units there now.
Picker and packer: label the bins
Hello {keeper}, please print and fix the bin label {label} for {product}.
Ops manager: below the reorder point
Hello {owner}, {product} is low: {available} available, {on_order} on order, point needed {need_point}. Suggested order: {suggest} units.
Hello, the count of {product} at {location} on {date} differs by {variance} units, a value of {variance_value}. Please decide: recount or accept.
Ops manager: no sale for a long time
Hello, {product} has had no sale for {days_since} days and {units} units are tied up, a value of {value}. Suggested action: {action}.
Hello {owner}, stockout risk: {product} runs out on {runout} at {daily} sales per day. The supplier lead time is {lead_days} days.
Hello {owner}, {product} is overstocked: {over_units} units above the target, worth {over_value}. Cover is {cover_days} days.
Hello {owner}, stock of {product}: {on_hand} units, value {value}, {cover_days} days of cover.
Owner: stock tied up in slow products
Hello, {product} ties up {value} with {days_since} days without a sale. Planned action: {action}; loss at the clearance price {loss}. Do you agree?
Hello, write-offs of {category} in {month} were {writeoffs}. The closing stock value is {value}.
Owner: buy for the peak season
Hello {owner}, for {month} we want {target_days} days of cover in {category}. Units short: {gap_units}, cost to close the gap {gap_value}. Please approve the purchase.
Hello, please confirm the arrival of {product} ({qty} units, order {po_id}). We expect it on {expected_date}.
Hello, {units} units of {product} were damaged or faulty ({reason}). Please send replacements or a credit.
Supplier: stock needed before a date
Hello, we need {suggest} units of {product} soon. Our stock runs out on {runout}. What is your first ship date?
Hello, can you split the delivery of order {po_id}? We need {product} ({qty} units) first, before {expected_date}.
Hello, we sent back {qty} units of {product} on {sent_on}. Please issue a credit note of {credit_expected}.
Hello {booked_by}, the closing stock value of {category} for {month} is {value} ({units} units). Please book it for the month end.
Hello {booked_by}, please book write-offs of {writeoffs} for {category} in {month}.
Marketing and content: plan a push
Hello, {product} is overstocked ({over_units} units above the target). Please plan a push: a bundle, a promotion or more ads.
Hello, {product} has {available} units available and {cover_days} days of cover. Please pause the ads if it runs out.
Hello {counter}, you count {category} in {location} on {date}. Please be there on time.
Stock take sheet to print for counters
Count plan {col:schedule.plan_id}: {col:schedule.category} in {col:schedule.location}, planned for {col:schedule.date}. Counter: {col:schedule.counter}.
The area holds {col:schedule.skus} products and about {col:schedule.units} units. Count what you see on the shelf and write it in the counted column. Never copy the system quantity.
Count each product once, then count it again if the difference is more than the recount limit of {set:approve_value}. Stop goods movements in the area until the count is closed.
Sign the sheet when every line is filled and give it to the warehouse lead.
Count plan {col:schedule.plan_id}: {col:schedule.category} in {col:schedule.location} on {col:schedule.date}, counted by {col:schedule.counter}.
{col:schedule.lines} lines were counted and {col:schedule.exact} matched the system. The accuracy is {col:schedule.accuracy}.
The net variance is {col:schedule.var_units} units, a value of {col:schedule.var_value}. Differences above {set:approve_value} on one line need a recount before the system is corrected.
The corrections are approved by the operations manager, and by the owner when a single line is large.
Our stock rules suggest {col:suppliers.lines} lines with a goods value of {col:suppliers.to_order}. Your minimum order is {col:suppliers.min_order}; the check shows {col:suppliers.min_check}.
Your lead time is {col:suppliers.lead_days} days and your past orders were late by {col:suppliers.late_days} days on average. We already have {col:suppliers.open_units} units on order.
Please confirm the lines, prices and the ship date by return message.

The closing stock is {col:valuemonth.units} units with a value of {col:valuemonth.value} at landed cost, or {col:valuemonth.unit_value} per unit. This is {col:valuemonth.share} of the stock value of the month.
The value changed by {col:valuemonth.change} since last month. Write-offs of the month were {col:valuemonth.writeoffs}.
The figures are booked by {col:valuemonth.booked_by} for the month end.
The last sale was on {col:dead.last_sale}, {col:dead.days_since} days ago. {col:dead.units} units are on hand and {col:dead.sold_90} were sold in 90 days. The stock covers {col:dead.cover} days.

The value tied up is {col:dead.value}. The class is {col:dead.kind} and the action is {col:dead.action}. At a discount of {col:dead.discount_pct} the price is {col:dead.clear_price} and the loss against cost is {col:dead.loss}.
Dead stock is reviewed every month and the decision is written here.
Adjustment {col:adjust.adj_id} on {col:adjust.date}: {col:adjust.type} of {col:adjust.qty} units of {col:adjust.product} ({col:adjust.sku}) in {col:adjust.location}.
Reason: {col:adjust.reason}. Reference: {col:adjust.ref}. The value is {col:adjust.value} at landed cost.
Approved by {col:adjust.approved_by}. Write-offs above {set:approve_value} need the signature of the owner.
Transfer {col:topups.transfer_id} on {col:topups.date}: {col:topups.qty} units of {col:topups.product} ({col:topups.sku}) from the main warehouse to the pick zone.
The load is {col:topups.cartons} cartons and {col:topups.weight_kg} kg, a value of {col:topups.value}. Moved by {col:topups.moved_by}.
The receiver checks the cartons and the count and signs below.
Expected: {col:openpo.qty} units on {col:openpo.expected_date}, a goods value of {col:openpo.value}. Stage now: {col:openpo.stage}.
Count the cartons and the units, note any damage and write the received quantity below. Receiving is done by {col:openpo.receiver}. Book the goods into stock within one day.

There are {col:stock.available} units available and {col:stock.on_order} on order. The stock covers {col:stock.cover_days} days at {col:stock.daily} sales per day. The target is {col:stock.target_days} days.
The units above the target are {col:stock.over_units}, a value of {col:stock.over_value}. The stock status is {col:stock.status}.
Please decide: stop reordering, run a promotion or bundle the product.
We want {col:cover.target_days} days of cover. At today's sales of {col:cover.daily_cat} units per day that is {col:cover.units_target} units. We have {col:cover.have_units} available or on order.
The units short are {col:cover.gap_units}; closing the gap costs about {col:cover.gap_value}.
Approved by {col:cover.owner}. Orders for the peak must be placed before the supplier lead time starts to run out.

Open Start and type your shop name and your own limits in the yellow cells: cover target, dead stock days, count difference limit, holding cost and the first day of the next peak.
Fill Products with your SKUs, cost, weight, reorder point and pack size, and Suppliers with lead times and minimum orders.
Enter the units in each location on Stock by Location. Stock by Product adds them up and shows available units, days of cover and the stock status.
Record what you reserve for open orders and the units sold in 90 days on Stock by Product. Open Orders feeds the units on order.
Set the safety days on Reorder Rules and read the suggested units, cost and run-out date every week.
Log movements on Stock Ledger and top-ups on Pick Zone Top-ups; use Bin Map to find each product and see which bins need filling.
Plan counts on Count Schedule and enter the counted lines on Stock Takes; accuracy and variance value fill in.
Book write-offs on Adjustments, graded units on Seconds Shelf and units sent back on Supplier Returns.
Review Dead and Slow Stock every month and use Seasonal Cover Plan before the peak.
Record stockouts on Stockout Log and month-end values on Stock Value by Month.
Use the 14 calculators for reorder point, order quantity, cover, safety stock, holding cost, peak build-up, count accuracy, clearance, top-ups, turns, space, overstock, stockout loss and order size.
Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to open your chat with the text ready.
Read Stock Dashboard and Charts every week.
Control purchase orders, suppliers, landed cost and payments
Control purchase orders, landed cost, suppliers and payments
ex-works cost plus the freight and duty rates of each supplier gives the real cost of every product before you set a price
Purchase orders with landed total and timing
every order shows goods, freight, duty, deposit, balance, days late, an on-time flag and a warning when it is under the supplier minimum
on-time rate, days late, defect rate, price changes and rating become one score, a verdict and a rank that use your own weights
what to order this week is grouped by supplier and checked against its minimum order value before you send anything
Payment schedule with deposits and balances
deposits, balances and freight and duty for every order with due dates, overdue and due soon warnings and cash needed for the next 90 days
defects found at the dock are compared with your highest acceptable rate and feed rejected units and credit expected
every claim is followed from open to credit received, with days open and a warning when a supplier is slow to credit
two or three offers for the same need are scored on price, lead time, quality and terms with weights you set
Lead time log with a safety buffer
promised against actual days per order show which supplier is late and how many safety days to add to the reorder point
the rate paid on each shipment is compared with the rate in the supplier terms so a high invoice stands out
invoice, packing list, transport and origin papers are counted for each order, and missing papers show before the goods arrive
lines still on the way show days to arrival and a late or arriving soon state, with messages to the supplier and the team

Suppliers: terms, lead times, minimums and rating
One row for each supplier with country, lead time, minimum order, terms, deposit, freight and duty rates and rating; orders, spend, average order and deposit per order fill in.
Product costs by supplier: ex-works and landed cost
One row for each product with its supplier, ex-works cost, pack size and reorder rule; landed cost with the supplier freight and duty rates fills in by itself.
Purchase orders: goods, freight, duty and delivery
One row for each purchase order with dates, goods, freight and duty; landed total, lead time, days late, on-time flag, payments and the supplier minimum check fill in by themselves.
Purchase order lines: quantity, cost and landed unit cost
One row for each product on an order with quantities, unit cost, freight and duty; line goods, landed unit cost, rejects and the cost change against the catalogue fill in.
Reorder proposals: what to order this week
One row for each product proposed for ordering with stock, sales and quantity; supplier, value, days of cover, arrival date and the order value against the supplier minimum fill in.
Open orders and arrivals: lines still on the way
One row for each order line still on the way with its expected date; supplier, value, days to arrival and the late or arriving soon state fill in.
Lead time log: promised against actual days
One row for each received order with the days promised and the days it took; the difference, the late or on-time state and the cause fill in.
Supplier payments: deposit, balance and freight and duty
One row for each payment with due date and the date paid; supplier, outstanding amount, days to due, status and the on-time flag fill in by themselves.
Quality checks at receiving: defects, rejects and credit
One row for each check at the dock with units checked, defects found, rejected units and credit; defect rate, the limit check and the reject rate fill in.
One row for each claim with reason, units, amount and status; product, days open, the claim state and the supplier phone fill in.
Supplier scorecard: lateness, defects, price and score
One row for each supplier with price changes; on-time rate, days late, defect rate, spend, share, weighted score, verdict and rank fill in from orders and checks.
Supplier price quotes: price, validity and answer time
One row for each quote request with the answer, price, validity and lead time; answer days, the fast-answer flag, change against the current cost and the quote state fill in.
Quote comparison: two or three suppliers for each need
One row for each supplier offer for a product need with price, lead time, quality and terms; the weighted score, rank and the best option fill in.
Freight and duty by shipment: amount and rate on goods
One row for each shipment with mode, weight and pallets; goods, freight, duty, the rate on goods, the supplier rate, the gap and the cost per kilogram fill in.
Minimum order and pack size rules by product
One row for each product with its minimum units, pack size, carton size and rounding rule; supplier, the rounded order quantity, its value and the check against the supplier minimum fill in.
Supplier contacts and visits: last call and next review
One row for each call, meeting or visit with the topic and the next review date; days since the contact and the review state fill in.
Sample requests: new product samples and verdicts
One row for each sample with purpose, cost, dates and verdict; product, days waiting and the sample state fill in.
Import documents checklist log by purchase order
One row for each purchase order with the dates each import document arrived; documents needed, received and missing, the due date and the state fill in.
Shipping mode and transit plan by purchase order
One row for each shipment with mode, carrier, departure and transit days; supplier, arrival date, days left and the transit state fill in.
The people who receive messages about orders, payments and receiving; one row each with role and phone.
